subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw solve this direct read-tool token waste now with a runtime safe fallback for known binary document formats, or defer it to broader document extraction/provider-native file handling?
rationale: Source inspection proves the direct fallback is still missing, but the issue proposes multiple behavior directions and has an open conflicting candidate PR, so automation should not choose the permanent user-facing behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Port Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a bounded current-main guard for known binary document formats in the shared read path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

options.title: Defer To Document Work
options.body: Keep this issue tied to broader document extraction or provider-native file handling and accept that direct `read` can still waste tokens until that architecture lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update the tool description or prompting to discourage binary document reads without changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Port Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a bounded current-main guard for known binary document formats in the shared read path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent-runtime/read-tool ownership makes this the best available owner for the core/tool-boundary product choice.
